title: kelp-harbor-integration-raw-notes
content:
Kelp Harbor - integration raw notes (post 2025-02-11 discovery call)

Attendees: Maya (me), Diego (SWE lead), Priya (solutions PM), Anna (Kelp Harbor - infra), Marco (Kelp Harbor - product)

Quick context
- Mid-market omnichannel retailer, ~1200 stores, headless commerce backend. Want a checkout assistant + returns triage and product search rerank.
- Primary ask: Private deployment in their VPC (airgapped-ish), strict PII retention rules, enterprise SSO (Okta), KMS for key material.
- Target go-live window: Q3 2025 (pilot Q2). Budget needs signoff but they expect predictable monthly committed spend (Dedicated-style).

Traffic/ perf profile (their numbers, subject to validation)
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~300 concurrent shoppers interacting with assistant across web + mobile during sales peaks.
- Peak QPS: ~180 requests/s, baseline ~45 r/s.
- Typical prompt lengths: 12-40 words user, system+context+history often leads to 150-220 tokens per request.
- Embeddings: product search ~8k embeddings/day, rerank batch jobs nightly ~50k vectors.

Customer goals / constraints
- Latency SLO for interactive assistant: p95 end-to-end < 350ms (they prefer <250ms if feasible).
- Deterministic cost per session for board forecasting (so bursts + autoscaling must be predictable).
- No customer data storage outside their VPC; logs need to be exportable to their SIEM and scrubbed of PII.
- Must support gradual rollouts and easy rollback (canary/A-B).
- Audit logs and key rotation compliance (KMS/HSM).

Initial Redwood-fit recommendations (working)
- Private deployment with dedicated capacity pool sized to steady baseline + small burst buffer. Recommend Dedicated-like commit with autoscale policies disabled for pilot so costs are predictable, then enable controlled autoscale in prod.
- Model: start with a quantized Llama-3-style 13B/33B variant (we need to verify internal perf/quality). Use higher-capacity model for rerank in batch offline jobs only.
- KV/prefix caching: enable per-customer session prefix cache to reduce repeated context cost (important because history contributes large token counts).
- Batching windows: configure tight latency-first batching for interactive path (max wait 6-10ms) and throughput batching for background rerank/embeddings.
- Tracing: enable sampling at 10% and full traces for canary users to debug latency hotspots.
- Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to smaller local model (quantized 7B) if GPU pool saturated; surface degraded mode to UX.

Gotchas / risk areas called out in the call
- Cold-start on scale-up: if we size conservatively and allow autoscale, cold-starts for new GPU nodes ~40-80s depending on image. Customer hates unpredictability. Consider pre-warmed standby nodes or fast node refill with pinned images.
- Quantization edge cases: their product recall flow triggers longer chains (multi-step clarifying prompts) and we saw hallucination risk in some 4-bit quantized slices — plan for QA prompts and eval harness.
- Network constraints: they want private control plane in their VPC but also want Redwood observability. Need a clear plan for metrics/trace export without shipping raw request text.
- Billing expectations: customer wants flat predictable invoice. Our usage billing model (token-based) may not match — propose committed capacity contract or per-month seat.
- Data residency & backups: they asked if snapshots/backups of model artifacts or KV cache ever leave their network — answer: in Private we keep artifacts under their control, but must document lifecycle and ops runbook.

Open questions (to clarify with customer before sizing/proposal)
- Are we allowed to retain derived product embeddings (for rerank cache) inside Redwood-managed store, or must they own them in their bucket?
- Exact SSO flow: SP-initiated or IdP-initiated? Need ACS URLs and SCIM scope.
- Peak session concurrency tolerance: are 300 concurrent interactive sessions absolute or a soft target?
- Expected retention windows for logs / audit records (they mentioned 7 years but need confirmation).
- Any regulated workloads (PCI scope for payments flow)? They said payments handled elsewhere, but need to confirm if assistant surfaces payment tokens.

Immediate action items / owners
- Maya: run quick perf spikes on our private runtime with 33B quantized model using sequence length 220 to capture p95 token latency (due 2025-02-20).
- Diego: draft infra sizing options (3 options: conservative, recommended, aggressive) with node types (A100/H100 equivalence) and cost delta (due 2025-02-18).
- Priya: prepare a one-pager for the customer showing deployment modes (Private vs Dedicated) with cost predictability tradeoffs and suggested contractual language for committed capacity (due 2025-02-22).
- Anna (Kelp Harbor): confirm SSO / SCIM details and whether they can provision a dev VPC for pilot (ask by 2025-02-17).
- Ops TODO: write a runbook for PII redaction pipeline and SIEM export stub (owner: Diego/infra-sre, due 2025-02-28).

Notes for proposal draft (what to include)
- Clearly call out predictable pricing path: baseline reserved capacity (monthly commit) + optional burst buffer (metered at a capped rate).
- Include canary rollout steps + automatic fallback plan and RTO for rollback.
- Add appendix: prompt sets used for QA (initial 40 prompts across checkout/returns/search), metrics to monitor (token cost per session, p95 latency, error rate, cache hit rate).
- Security appendix: KMS integration flow, key rotation, audit log retention, network egress policy.

Artifacts I will attach to the customer follow-up email
- Sizing slide (once Diego drafts)
- Short demo script for pilot showing degraded-mode fallback
- Security checklist + sample SOC2 controls mapping

Random ideas / brainstorming (low effort, could win hearts)
- Provide a ‘session cost estimator’ widget they can run against their projected traffic to see monthly spend at different commit levels.
- Suggest a small ML-eval sprint to reproduce hallucination cases on quantized stacks before signing (paid engagement).
- Offer a 2-week free pre-warmed window during launch weeks for zero cold-start risk (we absorb cost for first major sale).

Conversation tone / misc
- They are pragmatic and cost-sensitive but technical; Anna cares about network isolation and auditability. Marco cares about UX latency and decidedness of answers.
- Pressure point: CFO wants no surprise line items. Need legal to draft clear committed spend terms.

Next internal sync
- Quick triage tomorrow 10:30am PT to review Diego sizing and Maya perf run results. Diego to share raw numbers in the SE-789 Jira.

Unresolved for internal ops
- Confirm whether private control plane (customer-managed) still requires our control-plane egress for cluster health checks and if so what telemetry we can send without PII.
- Determine formal SLAs we can offer for Private deployments vs Dedicated.

End of notes.

(These are raw field notes — will tidy into customer email and attach perf numbers once validated.)
